rows.text: Thirty-two, one year left, and now the whole world takes turns. Fine. I'll make mine count.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: I've measured this forest twice and it moved in between. Who paints a continent and then shuffles it?
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Every flag's a note to the next crew: road's open, keep walking.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. The motto is only alluded to, never quoted.

rows.text: Another flag. If the next crew finds a straight road, they can thank me. If it's crooked, blame the dice.
Whoever painted this world gave it rules, a turn order and a scoring track. Very tidy. I'd still like a word with them.
Three pips. The arm's humming like the workshop the night before a deadline.
Overcharging. Everybody stand clear of the engineer.
Next stop on the road is right there. I want a workshop standing in it by nightfall.
The road reaches the Monolith's doorstep. Break it before morning, or I'm knocking.
Somebody pulled up my flag. Fine. Engineers rebuild.
You picked a fight with an engineer. I'll be taking notes on your weak points.
Halfway across the year. The number's lower, the road's longer, and I packed spare bolts.
Camp pitched at the Monolith's doorstep, flags all the way home. Tell Lumière to come and see.
Next expedition, then. Somebody write down where the road went.
Whoever painted this world has been at it for a very long game night. Somebody should check the clock.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: Somebody's mother has been playing too many board games, and we're the pieces. I'd still like to see her rulebook.
rows._notes: A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).

rows.text: Wheee! Somebody painted squares on the whole world! I'm much too round for squares.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Hmm! This rock is much too grumpy to be Florrie. Florrie is never grumpy.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Everyone takes turns now! I like turns. Turns are like waiting, but with a schedule.
Ooh, I think a rock is waiting over there. Hello, rock! I'm coming! Slowly!
Found you! In you go, safe and snug in the Big Belly.
One more friend home! My ring is getting all sparkly.
My friends are here! Thank you, thank you! Please be gentle with the guards.
rows._notes: The roster's 'Esquie's friends are here!' bubble, put in the first person because the roster keeps Esquie speaking in the first person until his in-game speech pattern is checked.

rows.text: Oof! That tickles. Not the fun kind of tickle.
rows._notes: Never Mad: he is hurt, never angry.

rows.text: Uh-oh, somebody's about to win! I'll go stand somewhere big and round and in the way.
Shh! Somewhere in the old city, a rock is snoring. I can hear it!
rows._notes: Act II tier: Dorrie hides in Old Lumière from Act II (story.act2.dorrie).

rows.text: Soarrie! You were with Mister Verso all along? You sneaky, floaty rock!
rows._notes: Act II tier, like story.act2.soarrie.

rows.text: All four rocks, all home! Everybody climb on and hold tight. We're going for a dive!
Whoever painted this world sure loves a long game! That's okay. I'm the MOST patient.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: Mister Verso says his mama has been playing too many board games. That's okay! I'm a VERY good piece.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).

rows.text: Hold still, darling. You're in the foreground.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. Her bot ends an announce turn with this line.

rows.text: Three easels, three faces I miss. Touch them and I'll paint you smaller.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Squares, turns, little wooden figures. If this is how the world must be painted now, I will paint it carefully.
The number on the Monolith follows your scores now. Play well, and watch it fall.
rows._notes: She paints the number; no line says she erases anyone.

rows.text: That clearing needs a little more of me in it. An easel, I think.
You've smudged a portrait. I'll start another. I always do.
The colours won't hold. Give me a moment.
rows._notes: Grief is Turmoil: kept quiet and sad, never mocking.

rows.text: Mind the canvas. The paint is still wet.
A ruined easel. I'll set up another and begin again.
Finished. Hold still, everyone, and let it dry.
rows._notes: Kept from implying she painted the people themselves, which safe mode must not say.

rows.text: One more round. The light is good, and the canvas isn't finished.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: Your father says I've played too many rounds. One more. Just one more.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).

rows.text: I foretold rain today. I did not foretell rabbits with opinions.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: The Aquafarm fed half of Lumière. This field can feed the other half.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Whoever's painting this world has let game night run a little long.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: New board, same job: keep the young ones out of harm's way.
Another Lantern lit and nobody trampling the crops. Don't worry, I'm counting.
That clearing has been noisy. I think it needs a Lantern and a little peace.
Every Lantern's lit. If you want them out, you'll have to come and put them out yourselves.
Those were seedlings. You can pay the farmer on your way out.
One Lantern down. I'll light it again. That's what Lanterns are for.
Half the year gone. I'll plant what I can while there's still light.
Twilight on the Aquafarm, a full harvest, and the children of Lumière watching from the shore. That's a good year.
rows._notes: Her grief is never played for laughs; Pierre is not mentioned in any line.

rows.text: I can't die, I can't leave, and now I have to wait for my turn.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Rank S. Please don't cheer. The moment I get proud, something hits me.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: A whole world laid out on a board. I've seen stranger things. Not many.
Up a letter. Keep it quiet; luck hears everything.
And there goes the letter. Nobody saw that.
That one's alone and slow. A clean fight. I'll take it.
Standing in the Monolith at S. Anyone who wants a different ending has one turn to land a hit.
Go ahead. I always get back up. It's the getting up that stings.
Here, old friend. It's been floating in my pocket all year. Fly safe.
rows._notes: Act II tier, like story.act2.soarrie.

rows.text: The last act. I know how stories like this end. Mostly.
rows._notes: Act II tier: vague, plays in either mode once the game reaches Act III.

rows.text: Quiet in here. I could get used to quiet.
rows._notes: His ending-flavoured win vignette is finished-only; this line stays neutral.

rows.text: Well played. I'll be here next time. I'm always here.
Whoever painted this world has been at the table a long time. At some point the pieces get to go home.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: Mother's been at this table for decades. At some point you let the pieces go home.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).

rows.text: Sixteen, and it turns out the whole world is somebody's board game. That explains a lot.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Everyone keeps asking what suit I am. I'm sixteen! I don't know what suit I am!
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: That's one more person who'd save me a seat at dinner. I'm keeping a list.
Feet planted, blade up. Your move.
Back to Lumière. For once, I'd like to be home.
I'm home, my friends are on my side, and my blade is sharp. Come and move me if you dare.
You'll have to get past the rapier first.
A memory just knocked. I'm not answering yet.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished Act III line below; matches safe mode's 'a memory returns'.

rows.text: The name was always under the paint. Alicia. Hello again.
rows._notes: Finished mode only; plays with her Act III portrait change (story.act3.alicia).

rows.text: Home, with my family around me. It took a whole board game, but here we are.
rows._notes: Her ending-flavoured win vignette is finished-only; this line stays neutral.

rows.text: Whoever painted this world plays like they've never lost a game. I'd like a word. Or a rematch.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: Wait. If she's my mother, who taught her to play like THIS?
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).

rows.text: My parents charted this ridge. It was not a ridge then. It was a lake. With otters.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Twelve clearings, three suits, perfectly balanced. Nature doesn't do that. Someone with a rulebook does.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Filed under 'Paintress, motives of': grief, regret, and apparently a strategy game.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Whoever painted this world wrote the rules down first. I would love to read the margins.
Recovered and catalogued. My parents would have argued with me about the date.
Their handwriting. Give me a moment. ...Right. Back to work.
The gold forest by Sirène. Escort of two, minimum. I am not losing these notes to a raid.
Mind the convoy. Those are primary sources.
Chart complete. The Monolith is circled, annotated and, frankly, overdue.
Revised thesis: whoever painted this world is very, very fond of board games. Peer review pending.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: Revised thesis: a grieving mother, a family quarrel, and far too many board games. Peer review pending.
rows._notes: A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).

rows.text: I would like your feet. Respectfully.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. Monoco speaks in the first person until his in-game speech pattern is checked.

rows.text: Mask changed! Today I am Heavy. Please mind the stairs.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Somebody painted us all into a board game? Wonderful. Which piece may I bite first?
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: A new foot for the wheel! Thank you, thank you. I will take very good care of it.
The river again. I remember... most of it. Splendid, let us begin again!
Five feet, five masks, the whole wheel spinning! Come and duel me before I finish dancing.
Oh! A challenger! Splendid, splendid.
Someone is about to win? Then someone owes me a duel first.
The wheel is full. Now, a quiet walk by the river with a friend.
rows._notes: Noco is only ever 'a friend'.

rows.text: Whoever painted this world loves games as much as I love duels. Good taste!
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: Esquie says somebody's mother has been playing too many board games. Too many? There is no such thing!
rows._notes: A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).

rows.text: Every game ends eventually. I'm simply ending this one on purpose.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. Plays as his win unlocks at Act III.

rows.text: I'm not the villain of this game. I'm the one who wants it to end.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: I'll be at the camp, sharpening things. Bring me your blades.
A small adjustment to your weapon. Don't thank me. Keep swinging.
rows._notes: The roster's 'the Curator upgraded your weapon' moment.

rows.text: Patience. The pieces are nearly where they need to be.
Lumière is mine to close. One more turn, and the curtain falls.
Break my camp and I lose a contact. Is that really worth your turn?
The curtain is down. Thank you all for playing.
Whoever painted this world should put the brush down. Some games should not last this long.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: Aline. Put the brush down. The children are watching you play.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).

rows.text: Another Nevron. Perfect? No. Next.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Some paint families. I paint teeth.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Now that is a perfect specimen. Hold still while the paint sets.
rows._notes: Her 'perfect specimen' bark on the first Convert of each other faction.

rows.text: A board, a manor, and plenty of empty clearings. I can work with that.
Another clearing with teeth in it. The tide is coming in.
That clearing has no Nevrons in it. Let's fix that.
Nevrons on every road and one at the Monolith's foot. By morning there won't be a colour left to save.
Break as many as you like. I'll paint more.
Whoever painted this world won't stop playing. So I'll make the board unplayable.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: She's been playing pretend in Verso's room for years. Somebody has to flip the board.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark. A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).

rows.text: Turn back. She is resting.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Expedition Thirty-Three. Next year, Thirty-Two. That's arithmetic, not cruelty.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: She keeps painting new players into the game. I keep taking them off the board.
rows._notes: Roster sample bark.

rows.text: Whoever painted this world made it a game of turns. Fine. I have always been patient at doors.
The shore road needs a closer watch. I'll be there before you are.
Every road to the Monolith is closed. You have one turn to find a way through. You won't.
Bold. Most expeditions turn back long before this.
The second act. My blade feels heavier. Not slower.
rows._notes: Unbeatable in Act I switches off at Act II.

rows.text: Nobody reached her. Nobody ever does.
Whoever painted this world never leaves a game unfinished. Neither do I.
rows._notes: Safe sibling of the finished line below.

rows.text: Your mother never could leave a game unfinished. I should know. I'm one of her pieces.
rows._notes: A finished-tier 'mother' line: finished mode only, and only in the mod's Act III (trigger.canvas-truth).
